title: Prohibition: Turns Out That America Loves to Drink
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with a recap of a trivia night at a rooftop brewery and a plug for the show's Facebook page and Twitter account. They then cover Prohibition in the United States: the temperance movement and its roots in the 1830s and 1840s, women's roles in temperance and consumer activism, the Women's Christian Temperance Union, Carrie Nation, scapegoating of German and Irish immigrants, World War One sentiment, the Eighteenth Amendment and Volstead Act, exceptions for medicinal and religious use, bootlegging, speakeasies, Al Capone, corruption, economic effects and the Depression, health effects, the repeal via the Twenty-First Amendment in 1933, and state and local dry laws including Georgia's Sunday sales ban and Alaska's dry towns. They compare international cases such as Finland's and Canada's prohibitions and Russia, and close with listener mail about a road trip and a request for a strange-sentence contest.
topics: Great Depression and alcohol tax revenue
Stuff You Should Know trivia night

segments.title: Trivia night recap and social media plugs
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck recap a trivia night at a rooftop brewery, miss a final question about second-best-selling album, and promote the Facebook page and Twitter account.

segments.title: Introduction to Prohibition and the temperance rationale
segments.summary: The hosts introduce Prohibition, also called the Noble Experiment, and explain that the temperance movement aimed to remove temptation for alcoholics. They discuss the social harms of alcohol that supporters cited, and note the Eighteenth Amendment's details and a grace year before it took effect.

segments.title: Early state bans and women in the temperance movement
segments.summary: Early state-level restrictions are described, including Massachusetts in 1838 and Maine in 1846. Women led much of the movement before they could vote, and the hosts mention their consumer activism.

segments.title: WCTU, Carrie Nation and the Prohibition Party
segments.summary: The Women's Christian Temperance Union was formed in Ohio in 1873 and the Prohibition Party in 1869. Carrie Nation is described as a militant activist who was arrested repeatedly for attacking saloons.

segments.title: Civil War, immigrant scapegoating and World War One
segments.summary: The Civil War briefly slowed the movement. Afterward, German and Irish immigrants were targeted as scapegoats, and wartime anti-German sentiment during World War One helped push Prohibition through Congress.

segments.title: Volstead Act, exemptions and near beer
segments.summary: The Volstead Act defined penalties and exemptions for medicinal and religious use, and defined intoxicating liquor as above 0.5 percent alcohol. Chuck shares a story about drinking non-alcoholic beer as a child.

segments.title: Effects of Prohibition: bootlegging, corruption and Al Capone
segments.summary: Speakeasies, bootlegging, rum runners, and political corruption grew. Bars and illegal brewing increased, enforcement failed in New York City, and Al Capone built a large criminal enterprise in Chicago.

segments.title: Economic and health effects, and repeal
segments.summary: Prohibition cost tax revenue, hit breweries, and worsened the Depression. Contaminated liquor caused deaths, and cirrhosis rates fell while overall consumption dropped. The Twenty-First Amendment repealed Prohibition, ratified December 5, 1933.

segments.title: Blue laws, dry counties and state holdouts
segments.summary: Georgia's Sunday sales restriction and blue laws are discussed, along with dry counties in Mississippi, Kentucky, and Alaska's dry towns. The hosts note some states held out on repeal and compare the cultural drinking patterns of Northern and Southern Europe.

segments.title: International prohibitions: Canada, Finland, Russia
segments.summary: The hosts compare other countries' prohibitions. Canada's lasted from 1918 to 1919, Finland's from 1919 to repeal in 1932 backfired, and Russia tried a brief experiment in 1914.

segments.title: Listener mail and strange sentence contest
segments.summary: A listener describes a road trip with a random podcast playlist and cites trivia from earlier episodes. The hosts respond to his School of the Americas suggestion and ask for listeners' favorite strange sentences.
